source.title: Platform Surveillance and Data Autonomy
source.description: Marlon from MIR gave a great talk at CounterSpy conf featuring Co-op Cloud 🎉 > How can we gain meaningful control over data in an era where instant collaboration and "cloud-based" applications are the norm? Why did the early internet dream of radically distributed networks turn into the centralized architecture of 2025? We will look at the infrastructure of the modern web - from humming server racks to law enforcement surveillance portals - and explore what it takes technically and politically to build autonomous data platforms for the needs of today's social movements. More info on counterspy.zip/archive and the MIR fedi.

editorial.why_selected: A CounterSpy conference talk from the Co-op Cloud project on platform surveillance and how cooperatives can run their own infrastructure instead.
learning_outcomes: How platform dependence creates surveillance risk for organizers
What cooperative hosting looks like in practice
editorial.try_next: Ask an organization you belong to where its member data is stored and who can read it.
